FOREWORD This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Power Line Carrier Systems and Associated Telecontrol Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council. This standard was originally published in 1980 and this revision has been undertaken to take into account the latest international practices in this field. In this revision, this standard is also largely aligned with IEC Pub 495 ( 1993) `Single sideband power line carrier terminals'. The complexity and extensive size of present-day electricity generation. transmission and distribution systems are such that it is possible to control them only by means ofan associated and often equally large and complex telecommunication system having a high order of reliability. The facilities which can normally be provided as part ofthe telecommunication system can be listed as follows: a) b) c) d) e) f) g) Telephony (operation, maintenance Facsmile transmission; Telegraphy; Telecontrol; Load frequency control; Teleprotection; and Data Transmission. and adminstration speech circuits);

The communication channels canbe provided by circuits leased from public facilities by means of utility-owned private circuits or, national regulations permitting, by a combination of both types or circuits generally calls for the provision of multiple routing, preferably be geographically diverse routes. In many countries, Power Line Carrier (PLC) channels represent a main part of the utility-owned telecommunication system. A circuit which would normally be routedvia a PLC channel may also be routed via a channel using a diffcrcnt transmission medium, such as a point to point radio or open-wire circuit. Since, in many casts, automatic switching is used, the actual rerouting,although predetermined, is unpredictable. It is important. therefore, that the voice frequency input and output criteria of all cquipcment used in the communications system are cornpatiblc. This compatibility is also beneficial in creating the ability to interchange and interwork equipment from different sources. This standard hasbeenprepared to enable compatibility between PLC links from different sources orbelwccn PLC links and other transmission media to be achieved and to define the terminal performance required in PLC networks. This standard covers basically 4 kHz and 2.5 kHz bandwidth modulation with single sideband transmission. The application of this Indian Standard to multichannel single channel PLC equipments that USCamplitude

cquipcment

is described in Annex A

For the purpose ofdeciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, obscmcu or calculated, expressing the result of a test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `RU~CS for the rounding offnumericalvalues (revised)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded offvaluc should be the s:me as that of the specified value in this standard.

IS 9482 : 1996

Indian Standard SINGLE SIDEBAND POWER LINE CARRIER TERMINALS - SPECIFICATION (First Revision)
1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard applies to Single Sideband (SSB) Power Line Carrier (PLC) Terminals used to transmit information over High Voltage (HV) Lines, and establishes recommended values for characteristic input and output quantities of single sideband PLC terminals ( see Fig. 1 ) and definitions essential for an understanding of these recommendations.
IS No.

Title

9528 ( Part 2 ) : 1980

Manual for planning of (SSB) PLC Systems: Part 2 PLC Systems planning

1.2 This standard covers two versions of the PLC equipment intended for two different applications as given below: a) Standard Terminal - Equipment with a voice frequency side interface which offers transmission of a frequency band of 300 Hz to 3 400 Hz on a four-wire basis plus signalling facilities. This equipment is capable via analog interafce, of being connected to networks that may consist of transmission equipment of different types and from different manufacturers. There may be facilities for additional point to point connection ( for example. a teleprotection connection ) which may fall outside the frequency band of 300 Hz to 3 400 Hz ( see Fig. 2 ). b) Speech-Plus Terminal - Equipment where specific interfaces for signals like speech, data and teleprotection are present at the voice frequency side ( see Fig. 3 ). The two versions will have parts in common and the requirements of these common parts are dealt with under 6.2 and 6.3.1. 2 REFERENCES The following Indian Standards are necessary adjuncts to this standard: IS No. 1885 ( Part74 ): 1993 Title Electrotechnical vocabulary: Part 74 Electrical and magnetic devices

6.2 Carrier Frequency Side 6.2.1 Carrier Frequency Range and Bands The typical carrier-frequency range is 40 kHz to 500 kHz and the manufacturer shall state the range of carrier frequencies within which the recommended values will be maintained. Parts of the range may be barred by national regulations. 6.2.2 Nominal Impedance,
Tapping Loss Return Loss and

The noise measured across the power supply terminals of the equipment shall not be great&- than 3 mV psophometrically weighted. The test circuit is indicated in Fig. 4. 5 STORAGE AND TRANSPORTATION CONDlTIONS 5.1 Storage Conditions The equipment, including its protection ( not the equipment itself ), shall meet during storage the requirements in IS 13736 ( Part 3/Set 1 ) : 1993, class lK5.
NOTES

The nominal impedance at the carrier-frequency interface shall be 75 R ( unbalanced ) or 150 Q ( balanced ). Other impedance values may be agreed between the manufacturer and the purchaser. The return loss within the nominal carrier-frequency transmit band shall be not less than 10 dB. The impedance outside the nominal carrier-frequency transmit and receive band shall be such that any other PLC equipment, connected to the same coupling equipment, shall not suffer from a tapping loss higher than indicated in Fig. 5. 6.2.3 Balance to Ground For carrier frequency interface of the balanced type the balance to ground shall not be less than 40 dEI at power frequency ( 50 Hz to 60 Hz ). The measuring circuit for the determination of the balance to ground is indicated in Fig. 6A. 6.2.4 Spurious Emissions The maximum permitted level of spurious emissions is indicated in Fig. 7 In order to measure spurious emissions, the transmitter shall be modulated by two sinusoidal signals of equal amplitude, the transmitter being terminated with a resistive load equal to the nominal impedance.

REQUIREMENTS FOR INPUT AND OUTPUT QUANTITIES OF PLC TERMINALS

6.1 General In all test procedures which require the use of a pair of PLC terminals, the carrier-frequency inputs and

IS 9482 : 1996 For equipment with a 4kHz basic carrier-frequency band the frequencies shall be 350 Hz and 3 300 Hz. For equipment with a 2.5 kHz basic carrier-frequency band the frequencies shall be 350 Hz and 2 300 Hz. The amplitude of the test signals shall be chosen so that each produces a quarter of the stated nominal carrier-frequency output power. The measurement shall be made with the aid of a selective level measuring set with an adequate bandwidth. It is necessary to ensure that the limiting action of the limiter, if any, does not occur when making this measurement. 6.2.5 Carrier Frequency
Level A in Fig. 2 or point R in Fig. 3 ) of a pair of PLC

terminals shall not exceed -55 &mop. The measurement shall be made in the absence of any signal transmission ( except for pilot signal or reduced carrier ). 6.3.1.4
Harmonic distortion

The harmonic distortion of a pair of PLC terminals shall be measured at the output ( point A in Fig. 2 or point n in Fig. 3 ). A test sinusoidal signal with a frequency of 350 Hz and a level of -3 dEIm0 shall be injected at the input ( point A in Fig. 2 or B in Fig. 3 ). The level of each component measured at the output shall be lower than - 40 dBm0. 6.3.1.5 Selectivity When a sinusoidal signal with a frequency of 300 Hz outside the nominal carrier-frequency receive band is injected at the carrier-frequency side ofa PLC terminal with a level of +lO df3m0, the level of the received signal at the voice-frequency side shall be less than -55 dBm0. When a sinusoidal signal with a frequency of 4 kHz or more outside the nominal carrier frequency receive band, for the 4 kHz basic carrier frequency band version, is injected with a level of +20 dBm0, the level of the received signal at the voice frequency side shall be less than - 55 dBm0. For the 2.5 kHz version the signal injected outside the nominal carrier-frequency receive band shall be 2.5 kHz or more. The test is carried out on a link by injecting the signal at the carrier-frequency interface of one terminal by means of an external signal source and a hybrid ( .sec Fig. 8 ). 6.3.1.6 Nommal impedance
and return loss

The carrier frequency levels of speech and signals shall be subject to agreement between the manufacturer and the purchaser. IS 9528 ( Part 2 ) : 1980 may serve as a guideline. 6.2.6 Frequency Accuracy The virtual carrier frequency shall not differ from its nominal value by more than il0 Hz. 6.3 Voice-Frequency Side The following requirements apply to terminals without compandors. Guidelines on the use of compandors are given in IS 9528 ( Part 2 ) : 1980. 6.3.1 Common Requirements The following are the requirements that are common to the two versions defined as `Standard terminal' and `Spech-plus terminal'. 6.3.1.1 Automatic
gain control

In the cast of a 30 dB change in carrier frequency signal level within the regulation range, the change in voice frequency receive levels of both speech and signals shall be less than 1 dB. The automatic gain control characteristic shall be coordinated with the teleprotection requirements. 6.3.1.2
Transmit /receive frequency difference

The nominal impedance of all voice-frequency inputs and outputs shall bc 600 R ( balanced ). The return loss shall not be less than 14 dB within the effectively transmitted frequency band. 6.3.1.7 Balance to ground For all voice frequency inputs and outputs the balance to ground shall not be less than 40 dB within the effectively transmitted frequency band, measuring circuits arc indicated in Fig. 6A and 6B. 6.3.1.8 7klephonr
srgnalling channel

In the pair of PLC terminals, the frequency difference between a voice frequency signal applied to the transmit end and the received at the receive end shall not exceed 2 Hz.

IS 9482 : 1996 The pulse distortion shall not exceed 10 percent when the signalling channel is operated at a speed of 30 bands. The signalling channel shall be operated by a potential free open or closed contact or by earthing at the transmit side ( point C in Fig. 2 or 3 ) and shall provide a potential free contact or earth at the receive side ( point C in Fig. 2 or 3 ). 72 V and 50 mA on a resistive load. 6.3.1.9 Limiter action The limiter associated with the channel shall produce a limiting effect defined as follows. The action of the limiter shall start between -3 dBm0 and 0 dBm for any sinusoidal signal of a frequency between 300 Hz and the upper frequency of the channel. The levels of the carrier-frequency output signal ( point G in Fig. 2 and 3 ) measured by means of a true rms non-selective level meter shall not exceed +3 dBm0 for an increase in the voice-frequency input signal to a level of +15 dBm0. 6.3.1.10 Teleprotection
interface

The insulation test shall be carried out with the equipements under test ready to operate, but not switched on. The EMC tests shall be carried out with equipments in operation. The equipment shall not sutfer permanent damage from the tests, and aher the test the equipments shall be checked for correct operation. 6.3.2 Standard Equipment
6.3.2.1 Frequency band

Both the standard terminal and the speech-plus terminal

may have separate interfaces for teleprotection signals. The interfaces may consist of voice-frequency inputs, voice-frequency outputs and control circuits. a)
Frequency band

The effectively transmitted voice-frequency band is 300 Hz to 3 400 Hz. Outside this band there may be available bandwidth for local point-to-point connection ( for example, for telephone signalling, teleprotection or data transmission ). 6.3.2.2 Attenuation
distortion

The nominal frequency band used shall be specified by the manufacturer. The inputs and outputs should preferably be decoupled from the other signal inputs and outputs.

b) Leveh
The maximum specified carrier-frequency output power for the teleprotection signal should preferably be obtained for any level between OdBm to -2OdBm at the teleprotection transmit input. For the maximum received teleprotection carrierfrequency level, the level at the teleprotection receive output should preferably be between the manufacturer and the purchaser.

6.3.3.6 Frequency

band above speech

band

To utilize the frequency band above the speech-band there are two different solutions: Broad-band solution, where the band limitation is carried out in the connected equipment. Attenuation distortion and groupdelay distortion shall be according to 6.3.2.2 and 6.3.2.3 for the applicable part of the frequency band. Band limited solution, where the manufacturer defines the eff'ective bandwidth. Attenuation distortion and group-delay distortion are subject to agreement between the manufacturer and the purchaser. and far-end crosstalk due to

Near-end and far-end crosstalk, due to signal channels, either individually or collectively in a pair of PLC terminals, shall not give rise to a weighted disturbance power level of more than -50 dE3mOpmeasured at the output ( point B' in Fig. 3 ) both for the near-end and the far-end PLC terminals. The test shall be carried out by injecting a single sinusoidal voice-frequency signals with a level of -8 dBm0 at point D in Fig. 3. The signal shall be slowly swept over the frequency band used. lf there is no continuously transmitted signal present in the frequency band above the speech band, a second sinusoidal signal with a level of - 8 dE3mO and a frequency of 3 300 Hz for the 4 kHz basic carrierfrequency band version or 2 300 Hz for the 2.5 kHz basic carrier-frequency band version shall be injected for the test. 6.3.3.5 Speech-levels The relative four-wire levels used for speech ( points

ANNEXA (Foreword )
PARTICULAR RECOMMENDATIONS FOR MULTICHANNEL TERMINALS

A-l SCOPE A-l. 1 These recommendations apply to multichannel

equals: A(dB) = L,,,, (dBm) - 15 dEI - 20 log (n) where
A = artificial line attenuation; L f,O,"= nominal carrier-frequency output power

equipments where the general requirements listed in 6 of this Indian Standard are not pertinent. A-l.2 For multichannel equipment the general requirements in 6 shall apply unless specifically amended or augmented in this Annex. A-l.3 The two versions defined in 1.2 may both be applicable to a multichannel equipment. In one multichannel equipment some channels may have `standard terminal' interfaces and others `speech-plus terminal' interfaces. A-2 TERMINOLOGY The definitions in 3 apply with these comments. A-2.1 Nominal Carrier-Frequency Band (see 3.1.3) Generallyeach one-way channel of a multichannel PLC equipment uses a band equal to the basis carrierfrequency band and these bands are adjacent so the nominal carrier-frequency band of the equipement has a bandwidth equal to n x B ( n = number of channels; B = basic carrier-frequency band). Generally, n is even 2,4 or 6 ). The transmit and receive carrier-frequency bands may be adjacent or non-adjacent. A-2.2 Carrier Frequency Output Power (see 3.3 ) Generally, the peak envelope power of an equipment is limited by spurious emissions due to the carrierfrequency output amplifier. In this case, assuming the same power for each channel, the ratio between the peak envelope power of the equipment and the peak envelope power of one channel is n*.
A-3 REQUIREMENTS FOR INPUT AND OUTPUT QUANTITIES OFPLC TERMINALS The recommendations in 6 apply with these changes and additions.

n

level; and = number of channels.

A-3.2 Nominal Impedance, Return loss and Tapping Loss ( see 6.2.2 ) The impedance outside the nominal carrier-frequency transmit and receive band shall be such that any other PLC equipment, connected to the same coupling equipement, shall not suffer from a tapping loss higher than indicated in Fig. 13. A-3.3 Spurious Emission ( see 6.2.4 ) In order to measure spurious emissions, the transmitter shall be modulated by a sinusoidal voice-frequency signal of 2 000 Hz applied simultaneously with the same amplitude to each voice-frequency channel interface, the transmitter being terminated with a resistive load equal to the nominal impedance. The amplitude of the test signal shall be chosen so as to produce a l/n' part of the stated nominal carrierfrequency output power of the terminal. The maximum permitted level of spurious emission is indicated in Fig. 14. A-3.4 Interchannel
Crosstalk Attenuation

The near-end and far-end cross-talk attenuation measured between points A, B, or D of a channel and point A', B'or D'of the other channels for the near-end terminal, and betweeen points A', B' or D' of the considered channel and points A', B' or D'of the other channels for the far-end terminal, in a pair of multichannel PLC terminals, shall be not less than 50 dFI (see Fig. 2 and 3 ). The test shall be carried out by injected two sinusodial voice-frequency signals in one channel in the absence of any other signal transmission.

A-3.1 General ( see 6.1 ) The artificial line shall have an attenuation in dEIwhich

19

IS 9482 : 1996

For equipment with a 4 kHz basic carrier-frequency band, the signal frequency shall be 350 Hz and 3 300 Hz, ( the 3 300 Hz signal being injected in the signalband in the case of a speech plus channel ). For equipment with a 2.5 kHz basic carrier-frequency band, the signal frequencies shall be 350 Hz ( the 2 300 Hz signal being injected in the signal band in the case of a speech plus channel ).

The amplitude of these test signals shall be chosen so that each one produces a l/4 nz part of the stated nominal carrier-frequency output power of the PLC terminal. The measurement shall be made with a selective level measuring set with an adequate bandwidth and shall include harmonics and intermodulation products. Limiting shall not take place when making this measurement.

TERMINOLOGY

B-l LEVEL NOTATIONS B-l.1 Power Ratios Decibels are used as a measure of the logarithmic ratio, to the base of 10, of powers, of voltages or of currents, which may aiso be referred to as levels. Power ratios are defined as follows :

Power Level

B-2 TEST LEVEL IN THE SPEECH CIRCUIT The test level in the speech circuit is the absolute power level at any point of the circuit when the reference point, generally, the origin of the system ( the virtual or physical two-wire send leg input ) is energized by means of a generator having an iutcrnal resistance or R ohms equal to the nominal impedance at the point of origin, and an e. m. f. lJ, equal to: [Jo=2 The test signal, unless frequency of 800 Hz. ~ v 1 000 " otherwise spccificd. is of a

The relative power level referred to the power level at a reference point ( generally the origin of the transmission system ) is defined by the expression: rcf Thus a power level of a X dBm will be measured at an x dBr point if a 1 mW test signal is present at a point of zero relative level, assuming that no limiting action is taking place. B-l.4 System Power Level The term X dBmo is used to indicate a power level of X dB above or below 1 mW at the point of zero relative level of the system, according to whether X is positive or negative, that is, X 613above or below the test level at any point of the system. 20 X&r= lOlog+

B-3 PEAK ENVELOPE POWER The ( carrier-frequency ) peak envelope power of a multiplex signal transmittter is the average power present during one cycle of the carrier-frequency at the highest crest of the modulation envelope. It is recommended that in order to determine the peak envelope power the transmitter should be modulated by two sinusodial voice-frequency signals of equal amplitude located within the effectively transmitted frequency band. The transmitter is terminated by a resistive load equal to it; nominal impedance and the limiter is not in operation.

IS 9482 : 1996 The amplitude of the modulation signals shall so be chosen as to satisfy the requirements for spurious emissions. The peak envelope power is then considered to be four times the power of one of these signals, selectively measured. B-4 RETURN LOSS The return loss Ae is a measure for the mismatch between the nominal impedance of equipment and its effective value observed at a particular frequency and is expressed by: A, = 20 log 1 where 2 = effectively impedance of the equipment; and R = nominal value of the impedance. $$ I (dW

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form without the prior permission in writing of BIS. Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and `Standards : Monthly Additions'.
